title: Most Kids Handed Exactly Eight
statement:
You have money whole coins to hand out to children kids. The rules:

  • All of the money must be handed out.
  • Every kid gets at least 1 coin.
  • No kid may get exactly 4 coins.

Return the largest possible number of kids who get exactly 8 coins. If the rules cannot be met at all, return -1.

examples.why: Two eights would leave exactly 4 for the third kid, which is forbidden. So: 8, 11, 1.
Both kids at 8 uses 16, and the last coin must go to someone. So: 8 and 9.
There is not enough to give every kid one coin.

hints: Give every kid 1 coin first. How many more coins does a kid need to reach 8?
With the leftover money, top up as many kids as possible by 7. What can go wrong with the money that remains?
Two cases spoil the count: everyone reached 8 but coins are left over, and exactly one kid is left who would end up with exactly 4.

explain.intuition:
Hand everyone 1 coin; if that is impossible, return -1. Now each extra 7 coins turns one kid into an eight. So the first guess is k = min(children, floor(rest / 7)). Any coins that remain go to the kids who are not eights, and since there is at least one of them, that is usually fine.

Only two leftovers break this. If all kids are already eights and coins remain, one kid has to take them and stop being an eight, so the answer is children − 1. If exactly one kid is not an eight and the remainder is 3, that kid ends with 1 + 3 = 4, which is forbidden; moving coins from an eight to fix it costs one eight, so the answer is k − 1. With two or more non-eights, any remainder can be split to avoid 4.
steps: Set rest = money − children and k = min(children, floor(rest / 7)).
pitfalls: Ignoring the no-four rule: money = 20, children = 3 is 1, not 2.
Making everyone an eight when there is money left over: money = 17, children = 2 is 1, not 2.
Forgetting the impossible case. With money = 1, children = 2 the answer is -1, not 0: zero eights would still require every kid to get a coin.

solutions.title: Try every count from the top
solutions.idea: For k from the largest conceivable value down to 0, check whether the other kids can share the remaining money under the rules.

solutions.title: Greedy with two corrections
solutions.idea: Give everyone 1, top up by 7 as often as possible, then fix the two leftover cases.

followups: The forbidden amount is now any number in a given list. How do you adapt the check for the last kid?
Maximise the number of kids with exactly t coins for a given t. Which parts of the formula change?
